notes: §1985:VII.3.4.4 GR3: "If the associated file connector is an external file connector, all CODE-SET clauses in the run unit which are associated with that file connector must have the same character set." Implemented at 85: BinderDriver.Bind keys every EXTERNAL file by its external name, so the entries share one connector; BindCodeSetClause resolves each clause's alphabet-name to its coded character set, and EmitCodeSetRegistration and RegisterCodeSet give the connector that set's conversion. The rule compares character sets, not names, and two alphabet-names for one set (the witness: STD1 and ASCII-CODE, both STANDARD-1) compile and run, as does an entry with no clause beside one with it (probed; 1985 constrains only the clauses present, where §2023:13.4.5.4 GR2 says "If any of the file description entries has a CODE-SET clause, all shall have a CODE-SET clause specifying the same character set."). Not implemented: the agreement. CheckExternalFileConsistency runs only under edition.DialectLevel >= 2023 and compares the FILE STATUS, RELATIVE KEY and LINAGE items only, and the descriptor EmitExternalDescribes renders for ExternalTable.Describe has no field for this clause, so no stage compares the clauses at any edition (probed at 85 and at 2023). Each program registers its own conversion on the shared connector at its first activation and the last one stands, so with STANDARD-1 in the program that opens the file and EBCDIC in the program it calls, the file is written in EBCDIC; with the two alphabets exchanged it is written in ASCII. kb/Work PB5069 holds the mechanism for two other clauses' rules; it does not list this rule id.

next.reason: 1985: "all CODE-SET clauses in the run unit which are associated with that file connector must have the same character set"; 2023: "If any of the file description entries has a CODE-SET clause, all shall have a CODE-SET clause specifying the same character set.". 1985 constrains only the CODE-SET clauses present. 2023 also requires every entry for the external connector to have CODE-SET once any has one, so mixing entries with and without it is refused.
